findings.summary: Intra-module call sites still name their target by the bare name, so a call that lexically resolves to an EARLIER shadowed binding gets a MUST edge to the LAST binding's row instead.
findings.evidence: build_local_fn_stamps stores (qualify ~prefix (Ident.name id), fn_arity vb.vb_expr) keyed by stamp but valued by the bare name; local_fn_name returns that bare name, feeding Head_local at lines 961 and 1317. resolve_local in arch_index.ml has no ordinal awareness. Probe: let f x = h1 x (row f#1); let mid_caller x = f x (line 4, lexically the f#1 binding); let f x = h2 x (row f). Indexed result: mid_caller's call lands on row f, not f#1.
findings.fix: Thread the binding_names table into build_local_fn_stamps so it stores bind_name (looked up by the same Ident.unique_name stamp key) instead of the bare qualified name. [Gate note: automated git-checkout-based red/green verification is structurally inapplicable here — the ratchet check (checks/mid-caller-shadow-attribution.js) was authored in the same review round as the fix it verifies, so no historical commit exists with the check present and the bug still active. pre_fix_sha intentionally left null (FR-034's flagged, non-blocking path) rather than pointing at a pre-check commit. Red-then-green verification was instead performed manually and is documented in briefs/shadowed-function-identity-impl.md and this review's specialist transcripts: reverting build_local_fn_stamps to the pre-fix bare-name behavior made the check's underlying tezt assertion fail with the exact wrong-attribution message; reverting back restored a pass.]

findings.summary: The Head_enumerated arg-escape edge uses raw Ident.name id rather than local_fn_name id, so a shadowed function passed as a callback is enumerated onto the wrong (last) definition.
findings.evidence: add_call (Head_enumerated (Ident.name id)) loc bypasses local_fn_name, unlike every other local-target site on this path.
findings.fix: Use local_fn_name id at line 941 — resolved by the same change as the HIGH finding once local_fn_name is shadow-aware.

findings.summary: On the LSP/flat path this change produces orphan caller names: functions rows there come from LSP document symbols with bare names, never renamed by build_binding_names, so a caller_name of 'f#1' joins to no row and is silently dropped by name-joining consumers.
findings.evidence: The flat schema's calls.caller_name has no FK and functions.name has no UNIQUE, so issue #41's row-collapse never applied on this path. Consumers join by name (bin/arch_serve/arch_serve.ml:379, :189), which now misses for a suffixed caller_name.
findings.fix: Revert this hunk in call_graph_extractor.ml — that path has no collision problem to solve, and renaming only the call edges (not the function rows) breaks the name-based join.

findings.summary: Test coverage gaps: no fixture has a caller between the two definitions (the case that fails, see the HIGH finding), none has 3+ same-name bindings, none pins exposed/doc attribution, none covers nested-module shadowing.
findings.evidence: Fixtures 2 and 3 both put the two 'let f' adjacent with no intervening caller, so no test exercises an inbound intra-module edge to a shadowed binding.
findings.fix: Add a mid-caller fixture, a 3-way shadow fixture, an .mli exposed/doc-attribution fixture, and a nested-module shadow fixture.

findings.summary: Fixture 3's headline assertion cannot actually detect an inverted ordinal direction; the direction is pinned only by the follow-up assertion at line 157.
findings.evidence: callee_names db ~caller:"use_a" = ["f"] can only ever return ["f"] or [] since a qualified call can only spell the bare name — it tests resolution-liveness, not direction.
findings.fix: Re-label the comment/error message as a resolution-liveness check and move the direction claim onto line 157; optionally strengthen by also asserting line_start/module path.

findings.summary: bind_base and bind_last are published in the .mli but read by no caller; bind_last is documented as if it were load-bearing.
findings.fix: Drop the two unused fields (binding_identity becomes bind_name only, or a plain string) or document them explicitly as informational metadata with no current consumer.

findings.summary: binding_identity's fallback docstring claims the branch 'should not happen' but it is reachable from call_graph_extractor.ml's unfiltered wildcard case.
findings.evidence: call_graph_extractor.ml's Tstr_value match has no Ident.name id <> "_" guard, unlike process_cmt's, so a ppx wildcard binding misses build_binding_names' table and hits the fallback for real (harmlessly, since qualify ~prefix:"" "_" = "_").
findings.fix: Correct the comment to state the fallback is exercised by call_graph_extractor.ml's unfiltered wildcard case rather than asserting it can't happen.

findings.summary: Function binding_identity shares its name with the type binding_identity.
findings.evidence: type binding_identity at line 704; let binding_identity names ~prefix id at line 749. Legal OCaml (separate namespaces) but reduces grep-ability.
findings.fix: Optional: rename the accessor function for readability.

findings.summary: build_binding_names and binding_name are exported but have no consumer outside arch_index_cmt.ml after the round-2 revert of call_graph_extractor.ml.
findings.evidence: Every call site is now inside lib/arch_index/arch_index_cmt.ml (lines 768, 780, 1587, 1683); the only external consumer was removed by this round's revert.
findings.fix: Drop both val declarations from arch_index_cmt.mli and keep the functions private, or note in the .mli they are exported for testing only.

findings.summary: Fixture 2c is described as covering exposed AND doc attribution, but only asserts exposed; the intent (doc) half has no assertion.
findings.evidence: register_exposed asserts only exposed db "f" and exposed db "f#1"; functions.intent (doc_tbl, keyed the same way) is never asserted, though verified correct by manual probe.
findings.fix: Add assertions on functions.intent for both rows in fixture 2c, using distinct .ml doc comments plus the .mli doc.

findings.summary: PRE-EXISTING, not a regression: a top-level binding with a type annotation (let x : t = e) produces no functions row, degrading calls to it to MAY_TOP.
findings.evidence: Confirmed pre-existing via a byte-identical 0-line diff of all function/call rows between the base commit and HEAD on a real 74-module corpus; the guard is untouched by this diff and both build_binding_names and the insertion pass skip the same bindings identically, so ordinals never desync.
findings.fix: Out of scope for #41 — track separately.

findings.summary: build_binding_names now runs twice per compilation unit — once inside build_local_fn_stamps and once directly in process_cmt.
findings.evidence: Both calls independently walk the whole structure; results are identical by construction so there is no correctness risk, only redundant work.
findings.fix: Have build_local_fn_stamps accept or return a shared binding_names table so process_cmt reuses it instead of recomputing.

summary: Round 2: all 8 round-1 findings (1 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM, 4 LOW/optional) verified fixed by both reviewer and architect specialists, independently and empirically (probe fixtures indexed through arch_callgraph_ocaml, a byte-identical 0-line diff of function/call rows on a real 74-module corpus, and a red-then-green re-verification of the HIGH fix). Full suite green (89/89). Four new LOW findings surfaced this round (dead public API surface, an untested doc-attribution half of one fixture, a pre-existing unrelated indexing gap for type-annotated bindings flagged out-of-scope, and a duplicate build_binding_names pass) — none blocking; carried forward as OPEN for a future pass. The HIGH finding's ratchet check (checks/mid-caller-shadow-attribution.js) could not be automatically red/green-verified by the gate's git-checkout mechanism due to a same-round check+fix commit topology; verified manually instead (documented in the impl brief and this round's specialist reports), and the gate's own flagged/non-blocking path (FR-034) was used rather than suppressing the note.
